Reels

Week 1: September 28 to October 4, 2026. 25 current Reel formats people are copying right now, each explained in plain words with ways to use it for your business. Pick the ones that fit; your This Week list says how many to film. Borrow the format and the text idea, and bring your own footage, buyer, and next step. We can't give you rights to any song: when the audio note says to swap it, swap it.
1This is your signReach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 25) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: Grab 5 to 8 seconds of everyday footage of your product, workspace, or finished result.

On-screen text: "This is your sign to [the thing you sell or fix]." End on one line with your next step.

For your business:

  • Handyman: a sagging gate + "This is your sign to finally fix the gate. Free quotes, link in bio."
  • Etsy tees: a folded tee on a Sunday table + "This is your sign to own one shirt that's just for doing nothing."
  • Photographer: golden-hour light in a field + "This is your sign to book the fall photos before the leaves drop."

No special audio: use your own voice, the natural sound of the work, or a cleared track.

2Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy…Reach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (SocialPilot report, Sept 10 to 24, 2026) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: One clip of your product or result, shown plainly, 5 to 8 seconds.

On-screen text: "Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy [your product or result]." Keep it light and specific.

For your business:

  • Bakery: a box of cookies opening + "…but it can buy a dozen brown-butter cookies."
  • Digital kit: an invite being edited in Canva + "…but it can buy a party invite you finished in 10 minutes."
  • Consultant: a clean project board + "…but it can buy a week without missed deadlines."

Trend audio: "Money Can't Buy You Happiness" (@eresdigna), about 125K posts (a creator's original sound). If Instagram shows it in the audio picker, you can try it; if not, or if you're unsure, the format works with your own voice or the natural sound.

3"Some people call me…"Reach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 11) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: Two or three quick clips of you at work, one per line.

On-screen text: List what people usually call you ("Some people call me the fence guy. Some call me Frank."), then land on "But you can call me when [the problem you solve]."

For your business:

  • Handyman: "…but you can call me when the fence starts leaning."

  • Etsy shop: "…but you can call me when you need a gift by Friday."

Trend audio: "Summer Love, Justin Timberlake". This is a commercial song: a business account may not see it, and seeing it isn't a license. Safe swap: keep the format, use your own voice or the natural sound, or a similar track from Meta's Sound Collection.

Carousels

30 carousel templates. Carousels do the Trust job: explaining, answering doubts, and proving. Every template follows the Playbook skeleton: slide 1 is the first hook, slide 2 is a second first impression (it has to make sense on its own), the middle proves it, and the last slide is the action. Make slides 1080 × 1440 (3:4), about 25 words or fewer each, and put the action on the last slide and in the caption. Examples use the Playbook's illustrative businesses.
1Problem → explanation → solutionTrust + Sell

Best for: Services that fix things

  1. Hook: name the problem the way the buyer says it
  2. Second hook: why it's worse than it looks (works on its own)
  3. What you check or look for first (real photo)
  4. When a simple fix is enough
  5. Proof: a before/after you have permission to show
  6. "Not sure which yours needs?"
  7. Action: your one next step

Example: Fix-It Frank: "Your fence isn't 'just leaning.'" → "If the posts are moving, the problem is underground." → … → "DM me a photo, or request a free quote from my profile."

Caption ask: "DM me a photo and I'll tell you if it's a repair or a replace."

Did it do its job? Look at DMs with photos, quote requests.

2Before → process → afterTrust

Best for: Visible transformations

  1. Hook: the "before," with one line
  2. Second hook: the result in one sentence
  3. Step 1 (real photo)
  4. Step 2
  5. Step 3
  6. The "after," same angle as the before
  7. Action: how to get the same

Example: Golden Hour Studio: toddler mid-meltdown → "the calm photo came 4 minutes later" → setup, warm-up game, the shot → "Pick your October date."

Caption ask: Your next step, in one line.

Did it do its job? Look at Saves, profile visits, inquiries.

3Objection → answer → proofTrust + Sell

Best for: Higher-priced offers

  1. Hook: the objection in the buyer's words, in quotes
  2. Second hook: your one-line answer
  3. Why that worry makes sense
  4. What you do about it
  5. Proof: a real review or result (with permission)
  6. What happens after they book or buy
  7. Action

Example: Golden Hour Studio: "'My kids won't sit still.' Good." → "The best family photos happen between poses."

Caption ask: "Booking link on my profile. Sessions are 45 minutes."

Did it do its job? Look at Saves, booking-page taps, bookings.

4Mistakes → consequences → fixTrust + Sell

Best for: Digital products and education

  1. Hook: "3 [thing] mistakes that [bad result]"
  2. Mistake #1 (works on its own)
  3. Mistake #2 and what it causes
  4. Mistake #3 and what it causes
  5. Your product fixing all three (screenshot)
  6. How easy it is
  7. Action with price

Example: Paper & Pixel: "3 invitation mistakes that make guests forget to RSVP." → … → "$25 kit, instant download."

Caption ask: "Comment PARTY and I'll send you the link" (only if you'll reply to every one).

Did it do its job? Look at Saves, comments, checkout visits, sales.

5Comparison: which one is for youSell

Best for: Two packages or two products

  1. Hook: "[Option A] or [Option B]?"
  2. Second hook: "It depends on one thing."
  3. Option A: who it's for
  4. Option B: who it's for
  5. Side-by-side: price, what's included, time
  6. The most common pick and why
  7. Action: link to both

Example: Sunday Supply Co.: "Just the tee, or the tee + tote bundle?"

Caption ask: "Both are linked on my profile."

Did it do its job? Look at Listing taps, orders, which option sold.

6Mini case studyTrust + Sell

Best for: Consultants and services

  1. Hook: the client's starting problem (no names without permission)
  2. Second hook: the real cause
  3. What you found
  4. The changes, one line each
  5. The result (real and approved, or labeled illustrative)
  6. "Which of these sounds like your team?"
  7. Action

Example: Ops Clarity: "An agency missing 1 in 4 deadlines." → "Missed deadlines are usually a handoff problem."

Caption ask: "Reply with the number that sounds like your team."

Did it do its job? Look at Replies, DMs, call bookings.

7Use case → result → productReach + Sell

Best for: Physical products

  1. Hook: the moment it's for
  2. Second hook: how it feels
  3. In use, place 1
  4. In use, place 2
  5. In use, place 3
  6. The product or bundle, with price
  7. Action

Example: Sunday Supply Co.: "The outfit for a Sunday with zero plans."

Caption ask: "Send this to your Sunday person." + "Bundle linked on my profile."

Did it do its job? Look at Sends, listing taps, orders.

17Things I'd never doReach + Trust

Best for: Anyone with expert habits

  1. Hook: "3 things I'd never do as a [job]"

Stories

30 Story templates. Stories are for people who already know you, and they're where warm people decide to buy. Each template is 4 frames: question or problem → proof or demo → answer or result → the ask. Use one sticker per frame, keep the link sticker inside the safe zone, and use urgency only when it's true. Save your best ones to Highlights.
1Quote nudgeSell
  1. Poll: "Anything in your house that's 'fine for now'?" (Yes / Definitely yes)
  2. An 8-second clip: a small problem that became a big one
  3. One line on what early fixes usually cost
  4. Link sticker: "Free quote, same-day reply"

Did it do its job? Look at Poll votes, link taps, quote requests.

2Real availabilitySell
  1. A favorite photo from a recent job or session
  2. A behind-the-scenes clip + question sticker: "What do you want to know before booking?"
  3. Real open dates (only if true)
  4. Link sticker: "Pick your date"

Did it do its job? Look at Link taps, bookings.

3RestockSell
  1. Question sticker: "Which color should come back?"
  2. Behind the scenes: packing the restock
  3. When it drops and any bundle price (only if true)
  4. Link sticker to the listing

Did it do its job? Look at Replies, listing taps, orders.

4DemoSell
  1. "[Deadline] and no [thing] yet?"
  2. A 10-second screen recording or demo
  3. A real review screenshot (with permission)
  4. Link sticker: price + "instant download"

Did it do its job? Look at Link taps, sales.

5Objection answered on cameraTrust + Sell
  1. Question box: "What stops you from [buying/booking]?"
  2. Answer the top reply on camera
  3. A real, approved result (or labeled illustrative)
  4. Link sticker: "Book a 20-minute call"

Did it do its job? Look at Replies, DMs, bookings.

  1. Poll: two options of your product
  2. Poll: two more options
  3. Show the winners
  4. Link sticker to the winning item

Did it do its job? Look at Poll votes, link taps.
